* Historical & Social Movements Collections: Curated resources on major events, strikes, and struggles—such as the [1926 general strike](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVgHrOzAV7H-x63-koIP0cC5bc1pmL9-OeveoMGRvjRYySlBPC_3eTrqkY2EdbvQaUKyIyQ4AGY0NU4ZIfOAcuVqXPqPZq-aTvoFrm4K9VBWXYyHWWSXf), the 1934 Minneapolis Teamsters strike, the Flint sit-down strike, the France 1968 protests, and modern movements like Black Lives Matter and Abahlali baseMjondolo. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVgHrOzAV7H-x63-koIP0cC5bc1pmL9-OeveoMGRvjRYySlBPC_3eTrqkY2EdbvQaUKyIyQ4AGY0NU4ZIfOAcuVqXPqPZq-aTvoFrm4K9VBWXYyHWWSXf)]

[[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXwHrOzAVbkhSTiOedWorE8h49u4wA-kV_3PLFqL4NE6oeks3ws7z6S7arVbzhwh2lqBxK8s3xhS5PGzRgUqBFY-TfRcs-PdN309sziVHCJkZtq5j6t2hMBbcdtfTbnA5)]
* Galleries: Visual archives featuring historical photographs, artwork, and poster collections from groups like [Up Against The Wall Motherfucker](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVOWgMnzD2MOURI4D82SwLgB_sStSRDrJ3GKq5bcFW_MEyUq-u-DH3KYLoR7KFTQSkO8LR5HldvKFIo6-gWJAxBNE_wHWI8CRmBbCLgHHZV6FUIDVUFZbr_M-eLw), [Black Mask](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVOWgMnzD2MOURI4D82SwLgB_sStSRDrJ3GKq5bcFW_MEyUq-u-DH3KYLoR7KFTQSkO8LR5HldvKFIo6-gWJAxBNE_wHWI8CRmBbCLgHHZV6FUIDVUFZbr_M-eLw), and British anarchist newspaper Class War. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZwHrOzAV2PpQU1KAt6ol58YUaPB5pDf8iTkQ2W7JYWIPaH8WuqX04z86-fAtdnNbOBwsqX5UsVZi6zLyzwtAYgL9nXGqhRB-A6XlfzFxd_ZMgAdMixeYO69DAph74AO-5OrDTcLj5c0), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVOWgMnzD2MOURI4D82SwLgB_sStSRDrJ3GKq5bcFW_MEyUq-u-DH3KYLoR7KFTQSkO8LR5HldvKFIo6-gWJAxBNE_wHWI8CRmBbCLgHHZV6FUIDVUFZbr_M-eLw)]

transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the Overview expanded, with its source cards
d: THE COLLECTIONS, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'Explore the libcom.org Collections to find an extensive digital archive dedicated to anarchist, libertarian socialist, communist, and radical working-class history.' Collections; biographies and thinkers; archives; galleries; reading guides. Six cards, all libcom.org.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the collections, the Overview walks the site's sections and names what each holds.
findings: THE SECTIONS AT THEIR GRAIN. Strikes, movements, writers, journals and galleries are given as the site's tabs give them, from the site alone.

THE CURRENTS AS NAMES. 'Emma Goldman, Anton Pannekoek, Amadeo Bordiga, CLR James, David Graeber, and Gilles Dauvé'. Pannekoek's council communism and Bordiga's left communism are the currents Lenin answered in 'Left-Wing' Communism (1920) and that lost their place in the Communist International; libcom keeps their texts. The composition lists them as 'prominent radical figures'.

NO HOLDER NAMED. The composition does not say who runs the library. The census's saved pages name no one; the site's own introduction, which its About link opens and the composition did not surface, names 'volunteer administrators' and states independence of all trade unions and political parties.
analysis: A faithful map of the site's sections. Who holds the library is on a page the composition did not surface, and the composition flattens the losing currents of the Third International into a list of figures.
per_note: The site cited throughout; no holder named.
